Consider the following differential operator:

D(y)=ydydx−2y

Fill in the steps in the reasoning below.

For any linear differential operator L, we have the linearity condition
L(ay1+by2)=L(y1)+L(y2)
L(ay1+by2)=aL(y1)+bL(y2)
L(ay1⋅by2)=abL(y1)⋅L(y2)
L(ay1+by2)=L(y1)+L(y2)
{(L(ay1+by2)=aL(y1)+bL(y2))(S0)} for functions y1(x),y2(x), and where a and b are constants.
